claims.claim: The Paley graph G_p is d-regular with d=(p−1)/2; adjacent vertices have (p−5)/4 common neighbors and nonadjacent vertices have (p−1)/4. Its adjacency spectrum is {d, ((−1+√p)/2)^((p−1)/2), ((−1−√p)/2)^((p−1)/2)}.
claims.evidence: Writing the nonzero-square indicator using the quadratic character and using Σ_x χ((x−u)(x−v))=−1 gives the stated adjacent and nonadjacent common-neighbor counts. Hence A²=dI+((p−5)/4)A+((p−1)/4)(J−I−A). On 1⊥ this becomes A²+A−((p−1)/4)I=0, yielding the two stated roots. Their multiplicities sum to p−1, and trace(A)=0 (equivalently, irrationality of √p) forces both to equal (p−1)/2. The checker independently confirms the p=5 specialization exactly.
claims.search_method: Direct quadratic-character and integer matrix calculation; exact p=5 checker as a finite endpoint check.

claims.claim: Every feasible degree-four moment matrix may be averaged so that its singleton principal block is N=[[1,a1ᵀ],[a1,aI+bA]], where pa is the objective and b is both the moment and diagonal pair-entry of every edge.
claims.evidence: Affine maps x↦sx+t with square s≠0 are graph automorphisms and are transitive on vertices and edges. Averaging their simultaneous index permutations preserves PSD, all union-consistency and clique-zero constraints, and the objective. Vertex transitivity makes singleton moments and diagonals equal to a; edge transitivity makes edge moments equal to b; nonedge entries are forced to zero. Union consistency gives M_{∅,e}=M_{e,e}=b for every edge e, proving the stated block and interpretation.
claims.search_method: Direct symmetry averaging and moment-consistency proof from the supplied SDP definition.

claims.claim: SOS_2(G_p)=√p, and hence the elementary hierarchy bound gives SOS_4(G_p)≤√p.
claims.evidence: Let q=(√p+1)/2, so the least adjacency eigenvalue is −q. For the averaged degree-two block, PSD on that eigenspace gives a−qb≥0, while PSD on the empty/all-ones span gives pa²≤a+db. Thus b≤a/q and pa≤1+d/q=√p (with the a=0 case immediate). Equality is attained by a=1/√p and b=2/(p+√p): the least-eigenspace and empty/all-ones determinant constraints are tight, and the remaining eigenspace is nonnegative. Every degree-four feasible matrix has a feasible degree-two principal block, so SOS_4≤SOS_2.
claims.search_method: Exact spectral decomposition and PSD inequalities.

claims.claim: For every finite graph G, SOS_4(G)≤1+max_v SOS_2(G[N(v)]).
claims.evidence: Set y_v=Ẽ[x_v] and R_v=Σ_iẼ[x_vx_i]. If y_v>0, L_v(f)=Ẽ[x_vf]/y_v is a feasible degree-two pseudoexpectation after conditioning: for linear q, Ẽ[x_vq²]=Ẽ[(x_vq)²]≥0, and the clique constraints restrict it to the closed neighborhood. Therefore R_v≤y_v(1+SOS_2(G[N(v)])). If y_v=0, the zero diagonal in the PSD singleton block forces its entire row to vanish, hence R_v=0. Finally PSD on the empty index and Σ_i x_i gives (Σ_v y_v)²≤Σ_vR_v. Summing the preceding inequalities and cancelling the nonnegative objective proves the claim, including the zero-objective case.
claims.search_method: Direct conditioning and PSD Cauchy–Schwarz argument for the stated moment model.

claims.claim: For nonzero f:F_p→C, |supp(f)|+|supp(f̂)|≥p+1; equivalently, every square minor of the p×p Fourier matrix is nonzero.
claims.evidence: For a k×k minor D=det(ζ^(x_i y_j)), order the distinct y_j and factor D as the ordinary Vandermonde in ζ^(x_i) times its integral generalized-Vandermonde quotient. Modulo π=1−ζ, that quotient is, up to sign, ∏_{i<j}(y_j−y_i)/(j−i), whose factors are all nonzero in F_p because k≤p. Thus D≠0. If a nonzero f had support sizes a,b with a+b≤p, one could choose b zeros of f; Fourier inversion on those rows and the b supported Fourier frequencies would give an invertible b×b minor forcing all Fourier coefficients to vanish. Conversely, a singular minor constructs such a violating function, establishing the stated equivalence.
claims.search_method: Cyclotomic generalized-Vandermonde proof and Fourier-inversion support argument.

claims.claim: Let P_- project onto the least-eigenvalue Paley eigenspace and let S_e consist of an edge e and all its common neighbors. With R=|S_e|=(p+3)/4, every real f supported on S_e and equal to 1 at both endpoints satisfies ||P_-f||²≥η₀:=2p^(−R)R^(−R(p−2)).
claims.evidence: The negative Paley eigenspace is one quadratic class of (p−1)/2 nonzero Fourier frequencies. If a nonzero vector supported on S_e lay in ker(P_-), its Fourier support would have size at most (p+1)/2, whereas R+(p+1)/2=(3p+5)/4<p+1, contradicting claim 4. Thus K=P_-[S_e,S_e] is positive definite. Cauchy–Binet gives det K=p^(−R)Σ_T|D_T|². For any chosen nonzero unnormalized Fourier minor D, its cyclotomic norm is a nonzero integer, while each of its other p−2 conjugates is at most R^(R/2) by Hadamard; hence |D|²≥R^(−R(p−2)). Therefore det K≥p^(−R)R^(−R(p−2)). Since K is a compression of a projection, all its eigenvalues are at most one, so λ_min(K)≥det K. Finally ||f||²≥2 from the two prescribed endpoint values, producing exactly η₀.
claims.search_method: Fourier-support injectivity, Cauchy–Binet, cyclotomic norm, and exact eigenvalue-product bounds.

claims.claim: For every prime p≡1 (mod 4), SOS_4(G_p)≤1+d/(q+η₀)<√p, with d=(p−1)/2 and q=(√p+1)/2.
claims.evidence: For a fixed edge e, let c be its singleton-to-edge column and δ=a−qb the singleton block's eigenvalue on the negative Paley eigenspace. Compressing the PSD moment matrix to that eigenspace and the e coordinate gives ||P_-c||²≤bδ. Here b=M_{e,e}≥0. If b>0, c/b is supported on S_e and equals one at both endpoints, so claim 5 gives ||P_-c||²≥b²η₀ and hence δ≥bη₀. Thus b≤a/(q+η₀). The empty/all-ones compression gives pa²≤a+db, yielding pa≤1+d/(q+η₀); if b=0 it instead gives pa≤1. Since 1+d/q=√p and η₀>0, the displayed bound is strictly below √p for every admissible prime.
claims.search_method: Exact compression and Schur-complement inequalities combined with claim 5.

claims.claim: If G is triangle-free and has an edge, then SOS_4(G)=2; in particular SOS_4(G_5)=2.
claims.evidence: For distinct edges e,f in a triangle-free graph, e∪f is not a clique, so the edge-edge block is diagonal with z_e=M_{∅,e}=M_{e,e}≥0. PSD of the block indexed by ∅ and all edges implies S=Σ_ez_e≤1. If t is the objective, PSD on ∅ and the sum of singleton indices yields t²≤Σ_{i,j}M_{i,j}=t+2S≤t+2, hence t≤2. A point mass on any actual edge is feasible with value two, proving equality. The exact checker confirms that G_5 is nonempty and triangle-free, so the specialization follows.
claims.search_method: General exact moment-block proof plus an exact-integer enumeration of G_5.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either fixed constants ε>0, C>0, p₀ proving SOS_4(G_p)≤Cp^(1/2−ε) eventually, or a rigorous disproof of that quantified statement. The draft proves only SOS_4(G_p)≤1+d/(q+η₀)<√p, where log η₀=−Θ(p² log p). Consequently its right-hand side is asymptotic to √p and does not imply any fixed-power saving; nor does an upper bound of this form refute the possibility that SOS_4 is much smaller. Nevertheless, the strict degree-four improvement and its supporting structural estimates are correct and material partial progress. The final writeup explicitly acknowledges this limitation, so PARTIAL is accurate and the draft does not overclaim target coverage.
